title: ASIR: Steganography for Diffusion Models via Antipodal Sampling and Iterative Recovery
claim: Extraction accuracy rises with signal separation between hypotheses, and our sampling shifts mass toward larger separations, yielding higher accuracy than random sampling.
layout: 1 panel, dual y-axes, accuracy curves with confidence bands over count histograms
description: A single matplotlib-style plot with a shared x-axis, the per-pixel signal separation, running from 0 to about 1.75. The left y-axis shows extraction accuracy from 0.4 to 1.0. The right y-axis shows sample counts from 0 to about 4000. Two lines show mean accuracy: a solid red line for Antipodal Sampling and a dashed blue line for Random Sampling. Each has a translucent shaded band for variance. Both curves climb steeply from about 0.5 and saturate near 1.0. The red curve sits clearly above the blue one at small and medium separations. Paired red and blue histogram bars show the sample counts per separation bin. They decay from left to right, and the blue bars are concentrated at small separations. A legend in the lower right names all four series. The eye goes first to the rising red and blue curves and the gap between them.
caption: Impact of Signal Separation on Extraction Accuracy. The x-axis represents the per-pixel Signal Separation (∆h,w = |x(0)
abstract: Messages embedded in diffusion generation noise suffer from severe attenuation due to denoising and VAE decoding, creating a persistent capacity–robustness trade-off. Identifying that extraction accuracy strictly correlates with the distance between candidate hypothesis images, we propose ASIR, a training-free and provably secure steganography framework for both pixel and latent diffusion models. ASIR introduces two key innovations: (i) Antipodal Sampling, which maximizes signal separation in probability space to enhance distinguishability, and (ii) Iterative Recovery, a paradigm shift that treats extraction as a gradient-based optimization problem to reverse non-linear distortions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ASIR achieves state-of-the-art performance, embedding up to 65,536 bits (pixel-space) and 16,384 bits (latent-space) with 99\% accuracy, while remaining statistically undetectable to deep steganalyzers.
